title: ML features without future leakage
summary: A Go feature store with historical training joins, Parquet offline storage, and Redis online serving.
decision: Only join features available at the prediction timestamp, within their validity window.

study.problem: A model can look excellent offline if its training features contain information that only became available after a prediction event. How can a feature store prevent that leakage?
study.built: Built a YAML feature registry, offline Parquet storage, online Redis serving, materialization jobs, and an HTTP API for online and historical feature retrieval. A PySpark path supports larger feature-computation workloads.
study.architecture: The registry describes entities, sources, and feature TTLs. Materialization populates storage. Historical retrieval groups feature rows by entity and selects the latest eligible timestamp for each event; online retrieval reads materialized values from Redis.

decisions.title: Time is part of correctness
decisions.body: Historical joins reject feature timestamps after the event and rows older than the configured TTL. An event with no eligible feature retains missing features rather than borrowing a future value.

decisions.title: Make serving paths explicit
decisions.body: Separate online lookup and historical join endpoints keep low-latency inference retrieval distinct from training-data construction.

decisions.title: Test consistency
decisions.body: Dedicated tests cover point-in-time joins, registry validation, offline storage, online storage, and consistency between serving paths.

results.label: Core guarantee
results.context: Enforced by explicit timestamp and TTL checks in the historical join implementation; this is an implementation property, not a performance benchmark.

results.label: Storage paths
results.context: Parquet for historical retrieval and Redis for online lookup, with a shared registry.

study.limitations: The historical join implementation reads source rows into memory and scans each entity’s rows per event. Spark materialization scale does not establish historical-join latency or online-serving capacity.
study.lesson: Training-serving consistency requires explicit time semantics, not just matching column names.
